findings.problem: The "False" explanation says "like me stuffing my crooked early stamps behind the takeout menus." That adds a new event to his backstory. In papa-dorin.md he slid to the back of the drawer behind the takeout menus himself, after the family stopped using him. He never hid his stamps there.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The "False" explanation says "I tried the back of a drawer for years, and I got found anyway." Saying he "tried" the back of the drawer makes it sound like he went there to hide or be alone. In his backstory he slid there because the family started using the new stamper. The Prep card for this stop (stop 1, card 9) gets it right: "I spent years at the back of a junk drawer, and I STILL got found."

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The "hide" explanation says "David spent a big chunk of this psalm finding out there's no hiding from the LORD. So at the end he prays..." The "So" gives a reason for David's prayer in Psalm 139:24 that the text doesn't give. It also links verses 7-12 to verse 24, a link the text leaves open.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Many right-answer explanations open the same way: the answer repeated in capitals, then "friend." Examples: "ALL of them, friend" (1/4), "BEFORE, friend!" (1/6), "He PRAISES, friend." (2/2), "BEFORE, friend." (2/6), "TRUE, friend." (1/14 and 2/15, word for word the same), "LEAD, friend." (2/17). After that opener, nearly every explanation follows "David says in Psalm 139:N, '...'" and then a bakery joke. Taken together, this reads as a formula. Vary the openers, and never repeat the exact same one.

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: Several jokes make up small events or habits at his bakery. Examples: "I turned off the bakery lights once to sneak a cookie and walked face first into the oven" (1/14 True), "I do all my secret cookie taste tests with the lights off" (1/14 False), "I hide one cookie behind the cookie boxes and can't find it myself the next day" (2/4 False) and "I tried counting the sprinkles in one jar" (2/8 True). papa-dorin.md encourages self-deprecating jokes but also says he never adds anything new to his bakery.
findings.question: Are made-up, one-off bakery anecdotes like these fine as self-deprecating humor, or do they count as adding something new to his bakery and Dorinverse story?
